analyses.name: EOG Resources, Inc.
analyses.verdict: A new 52-week high reached with an RSI of only 54.5 on the cheapest growth in the scan - a 10.4x forward multiple against 109% EPS growth - in the one sector where price, breadth and a live external catalyst all point the same way.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2025, ended December 2025)
financials.summary: EOG is the premium operator among US independent exploration and production companies, and the reason is structural rather than promotional. The company built its business around what it calls premium drilling: it only commits capital to wells that clear a demanding rate-of-return hurdle at conservative commodity price assumptions, which means its inventory is screened for economics before it is screened for volume. The consequence is that EOG generates free cash flow at oil prices where much of the shale complex merely survives. Its acreage is concentrated in the Delaware Basin and the Eagle Ford, with a growing position in the Utica, and it operates most of its own services in-house - sand, water infrastructure, and increasingly its own drilling and completion supply chain - which insulates unit costs from the service-cost inflation that squeezes peers when activity picks up. The FY2025 numbers reflect a business with substantial operating leverage to price: EPS growth of 109.4% on revenue growth of 58.7% means the incremental barrel drops almost entirely to the bottom line, because the cost structure is largely fixed once the well is drilled. That leverage is the whole investment case and also the whole risk. The balance sheet is among the most conservative in the sector - low net debt, a large cash position, and a capital allocation framework that commits a minimum share of free cash flow to shareholder returns through a regular dividend plus variable distributions and buybacks, rather than to volume growth for its own sake. Capital discipline in this industry is a cultural claim more often than a demonstrated one; EOG is one of the few operators for whom it has been demonstrated across a full cycle.
highlights: EPS growth +109.4% year over year - operating leverage on a largely fixed cost base
Revenue growth +58.7%, driven by realised price rather than volume expansion
Forward P/E of approximately 10.4x - the cheapest growth-adjusted multiple in the entire 474-name scan
Premium drilling hurdle: capital is committed only to wells clearing a return threshold at conservative price decks
Vertically integrated sand, water and completion supply chain, which caps unit-cost inflation
Conservative balance sheet with low net debt and a stated minimum free-cash-flow return commitment
Core acreage concentrated in the Delaware Basin and Eagle Ford, with an expanding Utica position

journey_52w.summary: The past year traced a move from 99.31 to 152.21 - a 53% advance from low to high - and it was not a straight line but a re-rating in two distinct phases. The first was fundamental: through the middle of the year the market gradually accepted that shale capital discipline was real rather than rhetorical, and that companies like EOG would harvest cash rather than chase production growth. That took the multiple from distressed to merely cheap. The second phase, which is what the last several weeks represent, is a supply-risk premium being priced into crude itself, driven by escalating pressure on Iran, disruption to Hormuz traffic, and attacks on Saudi infrastructure. The important detail is that EOG went to its 52-week high with an RSI of only 54.5, which means the advance has been gradual and absorbed rather than spiked - the opposite of what a headline-chasing move looks like. Energy now converts 15 of 20 names in the scan to STRONG BUY, the highest of any sector for a second consecutive session, and EOG sits only 10.1% above its 50-day, the least-extended of that entire leadership group.

critical.valuation: At roughly 10.4x forward earnings against 109.4% EPS growth and 58.7% revenue growth, EOG is the cheapest growth in the scanned universe on any measure that combines the two. The market is not paying for shale growth, it is paying a low single-digit-to-low-double-digit multiple for a cash-returning commodity annuity, and that is precisely because it assumes the current price environment is temporary. If crude holds, the multiple is too low; if crude reverts, the multiple is roughly right. That asymmetry - cheap on the current environment, fair on a worse one - is what makes the risk defensible, and it is why the position is sized on the 138.24 stop rather than on a price target.

analyses.name: Illumina, Inc.
analyses.verdict: A second consecutive new 52-week high, this one on 1.57x volume and with RSI still at only 56.2, delivered on the same day its own sector gave back 1.6% - the cleanest relative-strength signal in the entire scan.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2025, ended December 2025)
financials.summary: Illumina is a razor-and-blade business in the middle of a repair job. It sells DNA sequencing instruments and then earns the majority of its revenue and nearly all of its margin on the consumables and services those instruments consume for the rest of their working lives. That installed-base annuity is what makes the company structurally attractive and also what makes it slow to turn: when academic and pharmaceutical customers defer instrument purchases, the consumables base stops growing years before it starts shrinking. Revenue growth of 9.4% represents a return to expansion after a stretch of decline, driven by migration of the installed base onto the higher-throughput NovaSeq X platform, where per-run consumable pull-through is materially better than on the older generation. EPS growth remains negative at -9.4%, and the gap between recovering revenue and still-falling earnings is the whole investment question: it reflects the cost of running two instrument generations in parallel, restructuring charges, and residual drag from the GRAIL separation that consumed management attention and capital for years. The balance sheet is sound and cash generation from the consumables annuity funds the transition without external financing. What a 35x forward multiple pays for is not this year's earnings - it is the assumption that the recurring consumables line reaccelerates on a modernised installed base while parallel-generation costs roll off, which would move earnings far faster than revenue.

journey_52w.summary: From 91.00 to 213.24 is a 134% round trip and it is a turnaround story told in three acts. The stock bottomed when the market had priced Illumina as a structurally broken monopoly: instrument demand had stalled, GRAIL was consuming cash, activist pressure had arrived, and the competitive narrative around lower-cost sequencing rivals was at its loudest. The middle of the year was the repair - GRAIL separated, restructuring executed, and the NovaSeq X transition started producing measurable consumable pull-through rather than just slide-deck promises. The last two sessions are the third act: the stock broke to a new 52-week high on expanding volume, and critically it did so on a day when the rest of healthcare was giving back a 5.4% sector spike. That distinction matters more than the price. A stock making a high on volume while its sector unwinds is being accumulated on its own merits, not carried by a rotation. The caution is that the two-day move has pushed it 14.4% above its 50-day at 186.40, so the extension that was absent yesterday now exists.

If the consumables line stays at single digits, 35x is simply too expensive. The technical setup is what makes the risk manageable - the position is defined against 186.40, not against a valuation argument, and that is the honest way to hold it.

analyses.name: Freeport-McMoRan, Inc.
analyses.verdict: A volume-confirmed push into a new 52-week high in the day's best sector, with the strongest independent confirmation in the scan - TradingView STRONG BUY at 17 buy / 9 neutral / 0 sell - though revenue is contracting, which makes this a copper-price trade rather than an operating-momentum one.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2025, ended December 2025)
financials.summary: Freeport is one of the few genuinely irreplaceable assets in mining: a portfolio of large, long-lived copper mines - Grasberg in Indonesia, Morenci and the Arizona complex in the US, and Cerro Verde in Peru - that cannot be replicated on any relevant timescale. New copper supply takes a decade from discovery to first production and faces permitting regimes that have tightened everywhere, which means the marginal tonne of copper the world needs for electrification, grid buildout and data-center power infrastructure has to come from existing operators expanding brownfield capacity. That is the structural case, and it is why the stock trades on the copper price rather than on quarterly execution. The FY2025 figures are instructive about what is actually driving the shares: EPS growth of 28.1% on revenue growth of NEGATIVE 7.3%. Earnings improved while revenue shrank, which means the gain came from cost control, mix, and by-product credits - gold and molybdenum are meaningful secondary revenue lines at Grasberg - rather than from selling more copper. The Indonesian smelting and export arrangements around Grasberg have been a persistent operational and political variable for years, and they remain the single largest company-specific risk. The balance sheet has been repaired substantially from its leveraged past, and capital is now directed at brownfield expansion and leach-recovery projects that add tonnes at lower capital intensity than new mines.
highlights: EPS growth +28.1% achieved despite revenue growth of NEGATIVE 7.3% - a cost and mix story, not a volume one
Forward P/E of approximately 17.3x - a mid-cycle multiple for a commodity producer at a high price

journey_52w.summary: A double, from 34.96 to 71.55, and the arc has a clear logic. Copper spent the early part of the period as a cyclical proxy - traded on Chinese construction data and global manufacturing PMIs, and priced accordingly. What changed over the year is that the market began treating copper as an electrification and compute input rather than a construction input: grid buildout, transmission capacity, and the power infrastructure required by data centres all consume copper in quantities that do not depend on the housing cycle. That re-rated the whole group, and Freeport, as the largest listed pure-ish copper producer, absorbed most of the flow. The final leg is happening now: metals were the only place money went in the latest session, with FCX +3.14% into a new high on expanding volume and gold following through NEM +2.08%. The caution embedded in the chart is that gold's leader, NEM, closed with an RSI of 83.9 and sits 26.7% above its 50-day - a genuinely overbought condition in the adjacent metal that would drag copper sentiment if it breaks.

critical.valuation: 17.3x forward earnings is neither cheap nor demanding for a copper producer - it is roughly a mid-cycle multiple, which means the market is paying a normal price on the assumption that the current copper environment is normal. That is the crux. If copper is structurally re-rated by electrification demand against a supply base that cannot respond for a decade, 17.3x on a growing earnings stream is inexpensive. If this is a cyclical high in the metal, then earnings are at a peak and 17.3x on peak earnings is expensive. The negative revenue growth is the detail that should keep position sizing honest: the business is not currently growing, the commodity is.

analyses.name: Micron Technology, Inc.
analyses.verdict: The most extreme fundamental profile in the entire scan - 1368% EPS growth and 346% revenue growth at a 6.3x forward multiple - sitting 1.2% above its 50-day, which makes the invalidation line unambiguous. The catch is that semicap has not confirmed the bounce.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2025, ended August/September 2025)
financials.summary: Micron is one of three companies in the world that can manufacture DRAM at scale, and one of a small handful in NAND flash. That oligopoly structure is the entire reason the financials look the way they do. Memory is a commodity with no product differentiation and enormous fixed costs: fabrication capacity takes years and tens of billions to build, and once built it runs regardless of price. The result is a business that swings from catastrophic losses to extraordinary profits on relatively modest changes in the supply-demand balance, and FY2025 captured the up-swing in its most violent form. Revenue growth of 345.7% and EPS growth of 1368.5% are not typographical errors - they are what happens when a memory cycle turns from trough to boom against a fixed cost base. The demand driver is specific and, for once, structural rather than merely cyclical: high-bandwidth memory for AI accelerators consumes vastly more DRAM per unit of compute than traditional server memory, it is qualified years in advance with a small number of customers, and it is capacity-constrained rather than price-constrained. That has effectively removed a large slice of industry supply from the commodity spot market. The balance sheet was repaired through the boom and capital expenditure is now directed at HBM capacity specifically. The honest framing is that a 6.3x forward multiple is not the market calling this cheap; it is the market saying these are peak-cycle earnings that will not persist.

accomplishments: Rose +3.97% to 974.33 on a day Technology averaged -0.70% and QQQ closed below its 50-day

journey_52w.summary: From 115.60 to 1213.37 and back to 974.33 is one of the great round trips in the market, and the shape tells the story better than the numbers. The advance was the memory cycle turning: HBM demand arrived faster than anyone had modelled, spot DRAM pricing followed, and a business that had been loss-making re-rated from distressed to indispensable inside a few quarters. The decline from 1213.37 - a 19.7% drawdown - is the market beginning to ask the only question that matters in memory: is this the peak? That question is not answerable from the income statement, which is precisely why the multiple is 6.3x. What the latest session added was a bounce: MU +3.97%, MRVL +5.79%, STX +2.12%, a memory-and-networking-silicon rally off oversold levels. The reason to treat it as a bounce rather than a bottom is the group that did not participate. Semiconductor capital equipment - the companies that sell the tools memory makers buy when they are confident about the next cycle - stayed broken. AMAT closed flat and remains 31.4% below its high, KLAC is 38.3% below its high with a WEAK signal, and LRCX is 28.3% below. Memory makers bounce before semicap only when the bounce is technical. When it is a real cycle bottom, the tool orders come first.

critical.valuation: A 6.3x forward multiple on 1368% EPS growth looks absurd until you understand what it is saying: the market believes these earnings are the peak of a cycle and will decline. That is a reasonable base case for memory, and it has been right many times. The bull case is narrower but real - if HBM capacity for AI accelerators is genuinely supply-constrained and qualified years in advance, then a meaningful share of Micron's volume no longer prices like a commodity, and the cyclical multiple is being applied to a partly structural earnings stream. The trade is manageable precisely because the 50-day sits 1.2% below the close: you do not need to resolve the peak-earnings debate, you need only respect 963.04.

analyses.name: CSX Corporation
analyses.verdict: A 92.7 score with RSI 56.0 that closed green while its own sector fell 1.07% - and both other Class I rails did the same, which turns one stock's relative strength into a confirmed group move. It sits only 3.4% above its 50-day, the tightest structural stop of any 92-plus score in the scan.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2025, ended December 2025)
financials.summary: CSX operates a rail network across the eastern United States, and the essential thing to understand about a Class I railroad is that it is not really a transport company - it is a regulated infrastructure toll road with a franchise no competitor can rebuild. Nobody is laying new mainline track between the same city pairs. That gives the business unusual pricing power and unusually stable volumes, and it is why railroads trade at industrial multiples on utility-like predictability. The operating model is measured in a single figure, the operating ratio, and the discipline of the last decade across the industry has been to push that ratio down through precision scheduled railroading: longer trains, tighter schedules, fewer assets, less dwell time. FY2025 shows EPS growth of 22.7% on revenue growth of 10.1%, which is the signature of that model working - earnings growing at roughly twice the rate of revenue because the incremental carload moves over a fixed asset base. Volume mix matters: intermodal, coal, chemicals, automotive and agricultural products each behave differently, and coal in particular is a structurally declining but still cash-generative line. Capital allocation is straightforward and predictable - maintenance capex on the network, then buybacks and a growing dividend. The risk in a railroad is never the balance sheet; it is the economy that fills the cars.

journey_52w.summary: From 31.73 to 53.23 is a 68% advance, and for a railroad that is a substantial re-rating rather than a trading move. The driver was a combination of operating-ratio progress and the market's growing willingness to pay infrastructure multiples for franchise transport assets in a period when it was hard to find predictable earnings anywhere else. The last several weeks are more interesting than the year. Industrials as a sector has been deteriorating - it averaged -1.07% in the latest session, GE downgraded from STRONG BUY all the way to WEAK, CAT downgraded to WATCH, AXON fell 4.87% and HWM 3.46%. Through all of it the three Class I rails held: CSX +0.57%, UNP +0.74%, NSC +0.29%. Groups that hold while their sector breaks are where the next leadership tends to come from, and the fact that all three moved together rules out the single-stock explanation. CSX is the best-positioned of the three for entry because it sits only 3.4% above its 50-day, versus UNP's 6.5%, which means the risk on the position is defined tightly.

analyses.name: Reinsurance Group of America, Incorporated
analyses.verdict: The cheapest name in the buy list at 8.2x forward earnings, with 159.6% EPS growth, that closed green for a second session while its sector fell 0.93% - because a reinsurer earns on mortality spreads, not on the net interest margin that is currently breaking the banks.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2025, ended December 2025)
financials.summary: RGA is a life and health reinsurer, and that business is fundamentally different from anything else in the financial sector - a distinction that is doing real work in the current tape. A bank earns the spread between what it pays for deposits and what it charges for loans, which means falling yields compress its margin directly. A life reinsurer instead assumes mortality, morbidity and longevity risk from primary insurers in exchange for a share of premium, and earns on two things: whether actual claims experience comes in better than the assumptions priced into the treaty, and the investment return on the float held against future claims. Falling yields hurt the second of those over many years as the portfolio rolls, but they do not compress the first at all. That structural difference is precisely why RGA rose while COF fell 3.7%, SYF 3.6% and LNC 3.5% in the same session. FY2025 delivered EPS growth of 159.6% on revenue growth of 18.5%, a very large number that reflects favourable claims experience and the earn-in of recent transactions rather than a repeatable growth rate. The company has also built a substantial business in pension risk transfer and asset-intensive reinsurance, which converts blocks of in-force liabilities into long-duration, spread-earning assets. Reinsurance earnings are inherently lumpy - a single adverse mortality period resets a quarter - and an 8.2x multiple is the market pricing exactly that lumpiness.

journey_52w.summary: From 178.40 to 249.39 is a 40% advance, and for a life reinsurer that is a large move achieved without much drama - which is characteristic of the asset class. The year's driver was the earn-in of asset-intensive and pension-risk-transfer transactions plus favourable claims experience, both of which showed up in the 159.6% EPS figure. The genuinely relevant part of the journey is the last two sessions. Falling long-end yields have been compressing bank net interest margins, and the market has been selling banks accordingly: Financial Services averaged -1.2% one session and -0.93% the next, with COF -3.7%, SYF -3.6% and LNC -3.5% in the latest tape. RGA closed green through both. That is not a coincidence or a rotation artefact - it is the market correctly distinguishing between a business whose margin depends on the yield curve and one whose margin depends on how many people die relative to the assumptions in a treaty. Our prior read that the bank pullback was a buyable entry has not paid, and RGA is the position that expresses the same sector exposure without carrying that specific bet.

What makes it interesting now is not that the multiple is low in the abstract but that the business model is structurally on the right side of the thing currently breaking its sector. You are being paid 8.2x for earnings that do not depend on the net interest margin, in a month when the net interest margin is the problem. The 50-day at 229.01 defines the risk.

analyses.name: CF Industries Holdings, Inc.
analyses.verdict: Up 5.60% and still carrying an RSI of only 51.5 - an un-extended entry into a group that just turned. It upgraded outright from WEAK to STRONG BUY, the highest-scoring of 26 upgrades in a session that produced 65 downgrades.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2025, ended December 2025)
financials.summary: CF Industries manufactures nitrogen fertilizer - principally ammonia, urea and UAN - and the business is best understood as a spread rather than a product. Nitrogen fertilizer is made by combining natural gas with atmospheric nitrogen, so the cost side is essentially the price of North American natural gas and the revenue side is the global price of nitrogen. CF's structural advantage is geographic: its plants sit on cheap, abundant North American gas while a large share of the world's marginal nitrogen supply is produced in Europe on far more expensive gas, or in regions with unreliable supply. That cost gap is the moat, and it widens precisely when global energy prices rise - which is the connection between this position and the same geopolitical tape driving energy. FY2025 delivered EPS growth of 99.6% on revenue growth of 17.6%, the signature of a spread business where a modest revenue improvement produces a doubling of earnings because the cost base barely moves. The forward multiple of 12.0x reflects the market's correct scepticism that a commodity spread is a durable earnings stream. Capital allocation has been shareholder-friendly through the cycle - substantial buybacks funded by spread earnings - and the company has been investing in low-carbon ammonia capacity, which is a genuine long-duration option on ammonia as an energy carrier and marine fuel rather than only as a fertilizer input.

journey_52w.summary: From a 52-week low of 74.99 to a high of 136.34 and now 125.68 - the year was a nitrogen spread recovery followed by a consolidation, and the latest session may be the start of the next leg. For most of the period the agricultural complex was the market's least-wanted sector: crop prices were soft, farm income was falling, equipment orders were being deferred, and fertilizer demand was being rationed by growers protecting cash. That is why CF was rated WEAK in yesterday's scan despite having doubled its EPS. What changed in a single session was Deere's earnings print. DE rose 6.93% on 2.54x average volume - the largest volume expansion of any gainer in the scan - and the entire complex moved with it: CF +5.60%, MOS +5.04%, BG +2.24%, and CTVA upgrading off the bottom. A single earnings report is a hypothesis, not a trend, and that caveat is real. But the specific reason CF is the best expression of it is the momentum reading: a 5.6% day that leaves RSI at 51.5 means the stock moved from a depressed base rather than extending an existing run. Compare that to healthcare's leaders two sessions ago, which moved 5% with RSI already near 90 and gave it all back.

analyses.name: Eli Lilly and Company
analyses.verdict: Real growth at genuine scale - 47.7% revenue growth and 26.2% EPS growth - offered on a 2.71% down day, 2.7% below its high and only 6.0% above its 50-day. This is the risk-defined way to own healthcare after the sector gave back 1.6%.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2025, ended December 2025)
financials.summary: Lilly is the rarest thing in large-cap pharmaceuticals: a company growing revenue at nearly 50% at a scale where that growth is measured in tens of billions. The driver is the incretin franchise - GLP-1 and dual-agonist therapies addressing type 2 diabetes and obesity - and the reason it matters more than a typical drug cycle is the size of the addressable population. Obesity is not a niche indication; it is a condition affecting a substantial share of the developed world's adults, with cardiovascular, renal and metabolic comorbidities that are now being demonstrated as separate label-expansion opportunities in outcome trials. Each of those expansions converts a lifestyle-adjacent prescription into a reimbursed chronic therapy, which is what changes the revenue durability. FY2025 delivered revenue growth of 47.7% and EPS growth of 26.2% - note that earnings grew slower than revenue, which is the tell for where the money went: manufacturing capacity. Lilly has committed enormous capital to building and acquiring fill-finish and API capacity because for several years the binding constraint on this franchise has been the ability to make the product, not the ability to sell it. That capex compresses near-term margins and is precisely the right decision. Beyond incretins the pipeline includes oral formulations, which would remove the injection barrier and the cold-chain constraint simultaneously, plus Alzheimer's and oncology assets that the market currently ascribes very little value to.

journey_52w.summary: From 690.97 to 1280.34 is an 85% advance driven by a single question the market kept answering more favourably: how big is the obesity market, really. Each successive outcome trial and label expansion pushed that answer higher, and each manufacturing capacity announcement made the answer more collectible. The last two sessions are a useful illustration of what the stock is and is not. Two sessions ago, healthcare exploded - the sector averaged +5.4% on a competitor's cancer-vaccine data, MRNA rose 177% and MRK 12.6% - and LLY participated with a 4.5% gain. In the latest session that entire move partially reversed: healthcare fell 1.61%, MRNA gave back 23.5%, ISRG fell 5.8%, and LLY declined 2.71%. What that sequence demonstrates is that LLY is the sector's largest weight and cannot outrun a sector unwind, which is a genuine limitation. But it also means the 2.71% decline is a better entry than the price two days ago, on a business whose fundamentals have nothing to do with the catalyst that caused either move. Price is now 2.7% below the high with RSI at 63.8 and only 6.0% above the 50-day.

analyses.name: Amazon.com, Inc.
analyses.verdict: An RSI of 40.6 attached to an 87.3 score - the most oversold reading on any high-scoring name in the scan. You are buying 242% EPS growth from the bottom of its own momentum range because Consumer Cyclical fell 1.56% and took it along.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2025, ended December 2025)
financials.summary: Amazon is two businesses whose economics have almost nothing in common, and the market's valuation of the whole depends almost entirely on the smaller one. The retail business - first-party sales, the third-party marketplace, advertising and the fulfilment network - is enormous, low-margin, and its profitability has improved substantially through regionalisation of the logistics network, which cut cost-per-unit shipped after years of national-scale inefficiency. Advertising, which sits inside retail, is the highest-margin revenue line in the entire company and continues to compound because it monetises purchase intent at the point of decision rather than attention earlier in the funnel. AWS is the second business: cloud infrastructure, high-margin, and now the destination for most of the company's capital. FY2025 shows EPS growth of 242.3% on revenue growth of 19.6%, and the gap is the story - the retail cost base was substantially fixed while revenue grew, and the operating leverage flowed straight through. What complicates the near-term picture is AI capital expenditure: training and inference capacity requires enormous upfront investment in silicon and data centers, which depresses free cash flow conversion well before the revenue arrives. That is the same trade Microsoft is making. The distinction from a pure semiconductor position is that Amazon monetises compute as a service on a subscription-like basis rather than selling hardware into a cycle, which is why AWS exposure behaves differently from owning memory or accelerators outright.

journey_52w.summary: From 198.79 to 284.02 and back to 260.11 - the year's advance was the market recognising that the cost discipline imposed on the retail business was permanent rather than cyclical, and that AWS growth had reaccelerated. The pullback since is where it gets interesting. Amazon now sits 8.4% below its high with an RSI of 40.6, which is a genuinely depressed momentum reading for a stock with an 87.3 score. The immediate cause is sector rather than company: Consumer Cyclical was the second-worst sector in the latest session at -1.56%, and the reason was WMT, which fell 9.2% on 3.31x average volume on its earnings print and dragged the entire retail complex with it. That is a real signal about consumer spending and it should not be dismissed - roughly half of Amazon's revenue is retail. But there are two offsetting facts. First, AWS and advertising, the two highest-margin lines, are not consumer-discretionary in the same way. Second, an RSI of 40.6 on a mega-cap means much of that worry is already in the price, which is not true of most names in this scan.

analyses.name: Coca-Cola Company (The)
analyses.verdict: A new 52-week high on the same day its own sector fell 0.89% and WMT collapsed 9.2% - when the consumer tape breaks and the most defensive large-cap staple prints a high, that tells you where the money went.

financials.period: Last completed fiscal year (FY2025, ended December 2025)
financials.summary: Coca-Cola is a concentrate and brand-licensing business that most investors mistakenly picture as a beverage manufacturer. The company largely does not bottle, distribute or deliver its own product - it sells concentrate to a global network of independent and partially-owned bottlers who carry the capital intensity, the trucks, the warehouses and the labour. Coca-Cola retains the brand, the formula, the global marketing function and the pricing architecture. That structure is why returns on invested capital are extraordinary for a business with such modest growth: the capital sits on someone else's balance sheet. FY2025 delivered EPS growth of 16.9% on revenue growth of 6.7%, which is exactly the model working as designed - price and mix, plus concentrate economics and buybacks, converting single-digit revenue growth into mid-teens earnings growth. The portfolio has been deliberately broadened well beyond carbonated soft drinks into water, sports drinks, coffee, juice and increasingly zero-sugar variants, which addresses the structural decline in full-sugar carbonated consumption in developed markets while emerging-market volume still grows. Currency is a persistent and underappreciated swing factor because the majority of revenue is earned outside the United States. The dividend has been raised for decades without interruption, which is not a trivia point - it is the reason the shareholder base is stable and the reason the stock behaves the way it did in the latest session.

journey_52w.summary: A 41% advance from 64.35 to 90.54 is a very large move for a company growing revenue at under 7%, and understanding why it happened is the key to understanding the risk. This was multiple expansion, not earnings acceleration. Over the period the market has repeatedly sought predictable, non-cyclical earnings - first as a hedge against a slowing economy, then as a hedge against the narrowing of technology leadership - and Coca-Cola is the purest available expression of that. The latest session was the clearest single demonstration of the pattern in the whole year. WMT reported and fell 9.2% on 3.31x average volume, COTY fell 9.6%, Consumer Defensive averaged -0.89% and Consumer Cyclical fell 1.56%. Against all of that, KO printed a new 52-week high. That is not a coincidence: when the consumer tape breaks, capital moves to the least discretionary consumer exposure available, and a concentrate business with global pricing power and a decades-long dividend record is where it lands. The corollary, which matters for sizing, is that this positioning unwinds immediately if the market re-risks into energy and materials leadership.

critical.valuation: 25.7x forward earnings for 6.7% revenue growth is expensive in absolute terms and the market knows it - what is being purchased is not growth but the reliability of the earnings stream and the asset-light returns on capital that fund the dividend. That price is justified when capital is frightened and unjustified when it is not, which makes this a positioning trade as much as a business trade. It earns a place in the buy list because it demonstrated exactly that behaviour in the latest session, printing a high while its own sector broke. It should be sized with the awareness that its main risk is not a business failure but a rotation.
